title: interpret a derivative value with units, separating marginal rate, average rate and percent change.
stem: A bakery's total cost of producing n loaves of bread in one day is C(n) dollars. It is known that C(150) = 420 and C′(150) = 1.80. Which statement is the best interpretation of C′(150) = 1.80?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average cost of each of the first 150 loaves is about 1.80 dollars.
choices.rationale: The average cost per loaf is C(150)/150 = 420/150 = 2.80 dollars, which is a different quantity from the derivative C′(150).

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each of the first 150 loaves costs 1.80 dollars, so the total cost is 270 dollars.
choices.rationale: This treats the rate at n = 150 as a constant price for every loaf, and the resulting total of 270 contradicts the given value C(150) = 420.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Producing the 151st loaf adds about 1.80 dollars to the total cost.
choices.rationale: Correct: C′(150) is the instantaneous rate of change of total cost, in dollars per loaf, so the next loaf costs about 1.80 dollars more. The average cost is 420/150 = 2.80 dollars per loaf and the relative rate is 1.80/420 ≈ 0.43%.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The total cost is increasing by 1.80 percent for each additional loaf.
choices.rationale: C′ has units of dollars per loaf, not percent. The relative rate would be 1.80/420, about 0.43 percent per loaf.

title: interpret a derivative value with units, separating marginal rate, average rate and percent change. (variant 1)
stem: The number of bacteria in a culture is B(t) thousand, where t is measured in hours. It is known that B(5) = 60 and B′(5) = −2.4. Which statement is the best interpretation of B′(5) = −2.4?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At t = 5 hours the culture contains 2.4 thousand bacteria.
choices.rationale: The number of bacteria at t = 5 is B(5) = 60 thousand. The value B′(5) is a rate of change, not a population count.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At t = 5 hours the population is decreasing by 2.4 percent per hour.
choices.rationale: B′ has units of thousands of bacteria per hour. As a percent of the current population the rate is 2.4/60 = 4 percent per hour, not 2.4 percent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At t = 5 hours the population is decreasing at about 2.4 thousand bacteria per hour.
choices.rationale: Correct: B′(5) = −2.4 thousand bacteria per hour is the instantaneous rate of change at t = 5. It is negative, so the population is falling; it equals 4% of B(5) = 60 only as a relative rate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The population was exactly 62.4 thousand at t = 4 hours.
choices.rationale: B′(5) is an instantaneous rate and only approximates the change over the next or previous hour, so it does not give the exact value of B(4).

title: interpret a derivative value with units, separating marginal rate, average rate and percent change. (variant 2)
stem: A city's total daily water use is W(h) gallons when the day's high temperature is h degrees Fahrenheit. It is known that W(90) = 5000 and W′(90) = 120. Which statement is the best interpretation of W′(90) = 120?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city uses 120 gallons of water for each degree of temperature from 0°F to 90°F, a total of 10,800 gallons.
choices.rationale: This treats the rate at h = 90 as a constant rate over all temperatures, and the total of 10,800 gallons contradicts W(90) = 5000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A change of 1 gallon in water use corresponds to a change of about 120 degrees in temperature.
choices.rationale: The units are reversed. W′ is in gallons per degree, so it describes gallons of change in W per degree of change in h.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The city uses 120 gallons of water when the high temperature is 90°F.
choices.rationale: The water use at 90°F is the function value W(90) = 5000 gallons. The derivative W′(90) is a rate, not an amount.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the high temperature is 90°F, each additional degree increases daily water use by about 120 gallons.
choices.rationale: Correct: W′(90) = 120 gallons per degree is the instantaneous rate of change of water use with temperature at h = 90, so one more degree adds about 120 gallons. W(90) = 5000 is the amount itself.

title: interpret a derivative value with units, separating marginal rate, average rate and percent change. (variant 3)
stem: The charge of a phone battery is B(t) percent after t hours of use. It is known that B(3) = 55 and B′(3) = −12. Which statement is the best interpretation of B′(3) = −12?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At t = 3 hours the battery charge is 12 percent.
choices.rationale: The charge at t = 3 is B(3) = 55 percent. The derivative B′(3) is a rate of change in percentage points per hour.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At t = 3 hours the battery loses 12 percent of its remaining charge each hour.
choices.rationale: B′ is in percentage points per hour. Twelve percent of the remaining 55 percent would be only 6.6 points, so this misreads the units.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The battery has lost exactly 12 percentage points every hour since t = 0.
choices.rationale: B′(3) is the rate at one instant. It does not show that the rate was constant on [0, 3], so the earlier rates may have been different.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At t = 3 hours the battery charge is falling at a rate of about 12 percentage points per hour.
choices.rationale: Correct: B′(3) = −12 percentage points per hour is the instantaneous rate at t = 3, negative because the charge is falling. It is not the charge (55), a percent of the charge, or a constant rate.

title: estimate a derivative from a table with uneven spacing and state its units when the function is itself a rate.
stem:
Water leaks from a tank at a rate of L(t) liters per hour, where t is measured in hours. Selected values of L are given in the table.
t (hours):   0   2   5   9
L(t) (liters per hour):   40   34   22   14
Using the data in the table, which is the best estimate of L′(4), with units?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Correct: t = 4 lies in [2, 5], so L′(4) ≈ (L(5) − L(2))/(5 − 2) = (22 − 34)/3 = −4. L is a rate in liters per hour, so L′ has units liters per hour per hour: the leak rate is dropping by about 4 liters per hour each hour.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This uses the interval from t = 5 to t = 9, (14 − 22)/4 = −2, which does not contain t = 4. The estimate needs the interval that straddles 4.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: The change in L over [2, 5] is −12, but it must be divided by the interval length 3 to get a rate of change.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The number is right but the units are not. L is already in liters per hour, so its derivative is in liters per hour per hour.

title: estimate a derivative from a table with uneven spacing and state its units when the function is itself a rate. (variant 1)
stem:
The rate at which cars pass a toll booth is R(t) cars per minute, where t is the number of minutes after 7:00 am. Selected values of R are given in the table.
t (minutes):   0   10   25   30
R(t) (cars per minute):   18   24   39   33
Using the data in the table, which is the best estimate of R′(20), with units?

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: t = 20 lies in [10, 25], so R′(20) ≈ (R(25) − R(10))/(25 − 10) = (39 − 24)/15 = 1. R is a rate in cars per minute, so R′ is in cars per minute per minute.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: The change in R over [10, 25] is 15, but it must be divided by the interval length 15 to get a rate of change.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The number is right but the units are not. R is already in cars per minute, so its derivative is in cars per minute per minute.

title: estimate a derivative from a table with uneven spacing and state its units when the function is itself a rate. (variant 2)
stem:
The amount of medicine in a patient's bloodstream is M(t) milligrams, where t is the number of hours after an injection. Selected values of M are given in the table.
t (hours):   0   1   3   7
M(t) (milligrams):   0   50   38   22
Using the data in the table, which is the best estimate of M′(2), with units?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: The change in M over [1, 3] is −12, but it must be divided by the interval length 2 to get a rate of change.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: t = 2 lies in [1, 3], so M′(2) ≈ (M(3) − M(1))/(3 − 1) = (38 − 50)/2 = −6 milligrams per hour, so the amount of medicine is falling.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This uses the interval from t = 3 to t = 7, (22 − 38)/4 = −4, which does not contain t = 2.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This is the average rate over the whole table, (22 − 0)/7. It is a positive average over [0, 7] and ignores that M is falling near t = 2.

title: estimate a derivative from a table with uneven spacing and state its units when the function is itself a rate. (variant 3)
stem:
The height of a sunflower is H(d) centimeters, where d is the number of days after planting. Selected values of H are given in the table.
d (days):   0   4   10   14
H(d) (centimeters):   2   8   17   19

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The change in H over [4, 10] is 9, but it must be divided by the interval length 6 to get a rate of change.

title: decide direction and speeding up or slowing down from the signs of v and a.
stem: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = t² − 5t + 4 for t ≥ 0. Which statement describes the particle's motion at t = 3?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The particle is moving left and slowing down.
choices.rationale: Correct: v(3) = 9 − 15 + 4 = −2 (moving left). a(t) = 2t − 5, so a(3) = 1. Velocity and acceleration have opposite signs, so the speed |v| is decreasing: slowing down.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The particle is moving right and speeding up.
choices.rationale: V(3) = −2 is negative, so the particle moves left. This answer reads the positive acceleration a(3) = 1 as the direction of motion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The particle is moving left and speeding up.
choices.rationale: Speeding up needs v and a to have the same sign. Here v(3) = −2 and a(3) = 1 have opposite signs, so the particle is slowing down.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The particle is moving right and slowing down.
choices.rationale: This takes the direction from the sign of the acceleration. The direction comes from v(3) = −2, which is negative, so the motion is leftward.

title: decide direction and speeding up or slowing down from the signs of v and a. (variant 1)
stem: A cart moves along a track with velocity v(t) = 2t² − 9t + 7 for t ≥ 0. Which statement describes the cart's motion at t = 2?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cart is moving left and slowing down.
choices.rationale: At t = 2 the velocity is −3 and the acceleration a(2) = 4(2) − 9 = −1. Both are negative, so the speed is increasing, not decreasing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cart is moving right and speeding up.
choices.rationale: The sign of v(2) = −3 shows the cart is moving left, not right. Speeding up describes the change in speed, not the direction of motion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cart is moving left and speeding up.
choices.rationale: Correct: v(2) = 8 − 18 + 7 = −3 (left). a(t) = 4t − 9, so a(2) = −1. Same signs mean the speed increases: moving left and speeding up.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cart is moving right and slowing down.
choices.rationale: The cart moves left because v(2) = −3, and with a(2) = −1 also negative the speed is increasing, so both parts of this statement are wrong.

title: decide direction and speeding up or slowing down from the signs of v and a. (variant 2)
stem: A bead slides along a wire with velocity v(t) = −t² + 6t − 5 for t ≥ 0. Which statement describes the bead's motion at t = 4?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bead is moving right and speeding up.
choices.rationale: V(4) = 3 is positive, but a(4) = −2(4) + 6 = −2 is negative. The signs differ, so the bead is slowing down.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The bead is moving left and slowing down.
choices.rationale: The direction comes from v(4) = 3, which is positive, so the bead moves right. The negative acceleration is the reason it slows, not a sign of leftward motion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bead is moving left and speeding up.
choices.rationale: The negative acceleration a(4) = −2 does not mean leftward motion or a rising speed. The velocity v(4) = 3 is positive and opposite in sign to a(4).

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bead is moving right and slowing down.
choices.rationale: Correct: v(4) = −16 + 24 − 5 = 3 (right). a(t) = −2t + 6, so a(4) = −2. Opposite signs mean the speed decreases: moving right and slowing down.

title: decide direction and speeding up or slowing down from the signs of v and a. (variant 3)
stem: A particle moves along a line with position s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t for t ≥ 0. Which statement describes the particle's motion at t = 5?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The particle is moving right and speeding up.
choices.rationale: Correct: v(t) = s′(t) = 3t² − 12t + 9, v(5) = 24 > 0 (right). a(t) = s″(t) = 6t − 12, a(5) = 18 > 0. Same signs: speeding up.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The particle is moving right and slowing down.
choices.rationale: At t = 5 the velocity is positive and the acceleration is positive as well, s″(5) = 6(5) − 12 = 18, so the speed is increasing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The particle is moving left and speeding up.
choices.rationale: V(5) = 3(25) − 60 + 9 = 24 is positive, so the particle moves right. Position is positive, but only the sign of the velocity gives direction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The particle is moving left and slowing down.
choices.rationale: Both signs are positive at t = 5: v(5) = 24 and a(5) = 18. The particle moves right and speeds up, so neither part of this statement holds.

title: find total distance traveled from a position function by locating the times the particle reverses direction.
stem: A particle moves along a line with position s(t) = t³ − 9t² + 24t meters for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5 seconds. What is the total distance traveled by the particle on this interval?

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: This is the displacement s(5) − s(0) = 20. The particle reverses direction at t = 2 and t = 4, so the distance traveled is larger than the displacement.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This leaves out the middle leg from t = 2 to t = 4, where the particle moves 4 meters in the negative direction, and counts only 20 + 4.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This adds the positions s(2) = 20 and s(4) = 16 instead of adding the sizes of the changes in position on each leg.

title: read increasing or decreasing and concavity from a table of a rate of change, and describe it as speeding up or slowing
stem:
A cup of tea cools after it is poured. Its temperature is T(t) degrees Celsius at time t minutes, and selected values of T′(t) are given in the table. Assume T′ keeps the trend shown for 0 < t < 15.
t (minutes):   0   5   10   15
T′(t) (degrees per minute):   −8.0   −5.2   −3.4   −2.2
Which statement is true for 0 < t < 15?

choices.label: A
choices.text: T is decreasing and its rate of decrease is shrinking, so the graph of T is concave up.
choices.rationale: Correct: T′ < 0 in the table, so T is decreasing. T′ increases from −8.0 to −2.2, so T″ > 0 and the graph is concave up; the cooling slows down because |T′| shrinks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: T is decreasing, and T″ < 0 because T′ < 0.
choices.rationale: The sign of T′ tells whether T is increasing or decreasing. The sign of T″ comes from whether T′ is increasing or decreasing, and the table shows T′ increasing from −8.0 toward −2.2.

choices.label: C
choices.text: T is increasing, because the values of T′ are increasing.
choices.rationale: T′ is negative throughout the table, so T is decreasing. The fact that T′ is increasing says only that the graph of T is concave up.

choices.label: D
choices.text: T is decreasing and its rate of decrease is growing, so the graph of T is concave down.
choices.rationale: The size of the rate of decrease is shrinking from 8.0 to 2.2 degrees per minute, so the tea is cooling more slowly, not faster.

title: read increasing or decreasing and concavity from a table of a rate of change, and describe it as speeding up or slowing  (variant 1)
stem:
A social media account has N(t) thousand followers at time t weeks, and selected values of N′(t) are given in the table. Assume N′ keeps the trend shown for 0 < t < 12.
t (weeks):   0   4   8   12
N′(t) (thousands per week):   6.0   4.1   2.3   0.8
Which statement is true for 0 < t < 12?

choices.label: A
choices.text: N is decreasing, because the values of N′ are decreasing.
choices.rationale: N′ is positive throughout the table, so N is increasing. The values of N′ decreasing says only that the graph of N is concave down.

choices.label: B
choices.text: N is increasing and concave up, because N′ is positive.
choices.rationale: A positive N′ shows N is increasing, but concavity depends on whether N′ is rising or falling. N′ falls from 6.0 to 0.8, so N is concave down.

choices.label: C
choices.text: N is increasing and growth is slowing, so the graph of N is concave down.
choices.rationale: Correct: N′ > 0 so N is increasing. N′ decreases from 6.0 to 0.8, so N″ < 0 and the graph is concave down: followers are still rising, but more slowly each week.

choices.label: D
choices.text: N is increasing at a constant rate, because N′ never changes sign.
choices.rationale: N′ is not constant. It drops from 6.0 to 0.8 thousand followers per week, so the growth rate is changing even though its sign is not.

title: read increasing or decreasing and concavity from a table of a rate of change, and describe it as speeding up or slowing  (variant 2)
stem:
The water level in a reservoir is W(t) centimeters at time t days, and selected values of W′(t) are given in the table. Assume W′ keeps the trend shown for 0 < t < 9.
t (days):   0   3   6   9
W′(t) (centimeters per day):   −1.2   −2.0   −3.1   −4.5
Which statement is true for 0 < t < 9?

choices.label: A
choices.text: W is decreasing and the decline is slowing, so the graph of W is concave up.
choices.rationale: The size of W′ grows from 1.2 to 4.5 centimeters per day, so the level is falling faster each day. W′ is falling, which makes W concave down.

choices.label: B
choices.text: W is increasing, because the values of W′ are getting larger in size.
choices.rationale: W′ is negative throughout, so W is decreasing. A growing magnitude of a negative rate means the decline is speeding up, not that W increases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: W is decreasing, and W″ > 0 because W′ < 0.
choices.rationale: The sign of W′ tells whether W is increasing or decreasing, not the sign of W″. W′ is decreasing from −1.2 to −4.5, so W″ < 0.

choices.label: D
choices.text: W is decreasing and the decline is speeding up, so the graph of W is concave down.
choices.rationale: Correct: W′ < 0, so W is decreasing. W′ decreases from −1.2 to −4.5, so W″ < 0 and the graph is concave down; the level falls faster each day.

title: read increasing or decreasing and concavity from a table of a rate of change, and describe it as speeding up or slowing  (variant 3)
stem:
The amount of product formed in a chemical reaction is P(t) grams at time t minutes, and selected values of P′(t) are given in the table. Assume P′ keeps the trend shown for 0 < t < 6.
t (minutes):   0   2   4   6
P′(t) (grams per minute):   0.5   1.1   1.9   3.0
Which statement is true for 0 < t < 6?

choices.label: A
choices.text: P is increasing, but the growth is slowing, so the graph of P is concave down.
choices.rationale: P′ is rising from 0.5 to 3.0, which means the rate of growth is increasing. A rising P′ gives a concave up graph, not a concave down one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: P is increasing and growth is speeding up, so the graph of P is concave up.
choices.rationale: Correct: P′ > 0, so P is increasing. P′ increases from 0.5 to 3.0, so P″ > 0 and the graph is concave up: the product forms faster as time passes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: P is decreasing, because the values of P′ are increasing.
choices.rationale: P′ is positive throughout, so P is increasing. A rising P′ describes how the growth is changing, not the direction of P.

choices.label: D
choices.text: P is increasing at a constant rate.
choices.rationale: P′ is not constant. It rises from 0.5 to 3.0 grams per minute, so the rate of formation changes over the interval.

title: compare marginal cost with average cost to decide whether average cost is rising or falling.
stem: A manufacturer's total cost of producing q units is C(q) = 0.02q² + 5q + 400 dollars, and the average cost per unit is A(q) = C(q)/q. At a production level of q = 50 units, which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average cost per unit is increasing, because the total cost C is increasing.
choices.rationale: Total cost increasing does not decide the behavior of the average. The average cost falls whenever the extra unit costs less than the current average.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average cost per unit is decreasing, because the marginal cost C′(50) = 7 dollars per unit is less than the average cost A(50) = 14 dollars per unit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average cost per unit is increasing, because the marginal cost is increasing (C″(q) = 0.04 > 0).
choices.rationale: A rising marginal cost does not alone make the average rise. At q = 50 the marginal cost 7 is still below the average 14, which pulls the average down.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The average cost per unit is 7 dollars at q = 50, because C′(50) = 7 gives the cost per unit.
choices.rationale: C′(50) is the marginal cost of the next unit. The average cost per unit is C(50)/50 = 700/50 = 14 dollars.

title: compare marginal cost with average cost to decide whether average cost is rising or falling. (variant 1)
stem: A print shop's total cost of making q posters is C(q) = 0.05q² + 3q + 500 dollars, and the average cost per poster is A(q) = C(q)/q. At a production level of q = 60 posters, which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average cost per poster is decreasing, because the marginal cost C′(60) = 9 dollars per poster is less than the average cost A(60) ≈ 14.33 dollars per poster.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average cost per poster is increasing, because the total cost C is increasing.
choices.rationale: Total cost increasing does not decide whether the average rises. The average falls whenever the cost of one more poster is below the current average.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average cost per poster is increasing, because the marginal cost is increasing (C″(q) = 0.1 > 0).
choices.rationale: A rising marginal cost does not alone make the average rise. At q = 60 the marginal cost 9 is below the average 14.33, which pulls the average down.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The average cost per poster is 9 dollars at q = 60, because C′(60) = 9 gives the cost per poster.
choices.rationale: C′(60) is the marginal cost of the next poster. The average cost per poster is C(60)/60 = 860/60, about 14.33 dollars.

title: compare marginal cost with average cost to decide whether average cost is rising or falling. (variant 2)
stem: A bike shop's total cost of assembling q bikes in a month is C(q) = 0.5q² + 4q + 50 dollars, and the average cost per bike is A(q) = C(q)/q. At a production level of q = 20 bikes, which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average cost per bike is decreasing, because the total cost C is increasing at a slowing pace.
choices.rationale: The total cost's growth is speeding up, since C″(q) = 1 > 0, and the extra bike costs more than the average, so the average is rising.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The average cost per bike is increasing, because the marginal cost C′(20) = 24 dollars per bike is greater than the average cost A(20) = 16.50 dollars per bike.

choices.label: C

title: build a relationship from similar triangles and differentiate it with respect to time.

choices.label: C

The tangent line to the graph of f at x = 4 is used to approximate f(4.3). Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The approximation is 6.4, and it is an overestimate of f(4.3).
choices.rationale: The values of f′ increase from −2.0 to −1.1, so f is concave up on this interval and the tangent line lies below the graph, giving an underestimate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The approximation is 7.6, and it is an overestimate of f(4.3).

choices.rationale: Correct: L(4.3) = f(4) + f′(4)(4.3 − 4) = 7 + (−2.0)(0.3) = 6.4. The values of f′ are increasing, so f″ > 0, the graph is concave up, and the tangent line lies below it: 6.4 underestimates f(4.3).
